title: Daemonologie
credit: King James I, 1597. Public domain. The Forgotten Books scan in update_01 has no extractable text, so this desk ships original notes on the 1597 treatise, not that reprint.

sections.title: Three books, 1597
paragraphs: James VI of Scotland, later James I of England, published Daemonologie in 1597 as a dialogue against those who said witchcraft was only a fable. The work is public domain. This desk does not reprint a modern facsimile.
The treatise has three books. The first treats magic and unlawful arts. The second treats witchcraft and the pact. The third treats spirits, fairies, and what James called the devil’s illusions.

sections.title: Beside Scripture
paragraphs: Deuteronomy 18:10–12 forbids a consulter of familiar spirits. 1 Samuel 28 is Saul and the woman at Endor. Acts 19:19 is books of curious arts burned at Ephesus. Read those verses in the Bible window. James’s 1597 argument is a royal study, not Torah.

sections.title: Names of powers
paragraphs: Strong’s on this desk keeps a short original glossary of names that appear in Scripture. Daemonologie is a later Christian king’s book about those names. Open Strong’s, then Extra-canon, and keep the shelves labeled.
